chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Mukhtār, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Should a man enter ihram in a black garment?” He said: “He should not enter ihram in the black garment, nor should he be shrouded in it.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ الْأَسْوَدِ: the black garment specifically mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: Can a man enter ihram in a black garment or be shrouded in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the dislike or prohibition of using a black garment for entering ihram and for shrouding the deceased. It reflects juristic guidance on prescribed religious dress in acts of worship and at death.
